newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lafarge first half net profit slumps.
newsitem.headline: Lafarge first half net profit slumps.

text.p: French building materials company Lafarge said on Wednesday net profit for the first six months had halved from a year ago but it forecast a rebound in the second half.

Lafarge reported net attributable profit for the first half of 545 million francs, down from 1.15 billion francs a year ago, and blamed a combination of severe winter weather, weakness in mature markets and a near absence of exceptional gains.

But chairman Bertrand Collomb said in a statement the first half figures were not representative for the full year and the company saw encouraging signs of recovery in some markets which should mean it would post operating profits similar to 1995.
"The second half should...be better than the first and our objective is to reach an annual operating profit, excluding exceptionals, similar to that of last year," he said.

Lafarge posted full-year 1995 operating profit, excluding exceptionals, of 4.04 billion francs, on turnover of 33.22 billion francs. The company made a 1995 net attributable profit of 2.35 billion francs.
Collomb said the first quarter of 1996 had been "particularly difficult," with a severe winter which led to a loss in volumes.

The second quarter was one of contrasts -- weakness in France, where the construction industry saw the most difficult conditions for a long time, a mediocre western European market, strength in the United States and excellent conditions in some emerging markets.
Collomb said it was the unusual coincidence of these factors and the absence of exceptional elements which lay behind the fall in first-half results.
Lafarge will pursue its policy of expansion which would allow it to benefit from the dynamism of certain markets, he said.
Lafarge made an exceptional gain of 429 million francs a year ago from the sale of its stake in U.S. company National Gypsum but only posted an exceptional gain of 47 million this time round.

Lafarge posted first-half turnover of 15.88 billion francs, compared to 15.95 billion a year ago. Shareholder equity stood at 31,572 million francs at end-June compared to 30,794 million at the end of 1995. Net debt was 4,369 million francs, up from 2,938 million at end-December.
